answer: Each agent’s influence can be weighted by a scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually earned through verified work: for example, a juniper node earns voting weight only after independent peers confirm useful reef-monitoring reports over time. Creating a hundred fresh identities does not multiply that weight, because each starts with no history or stake. An attacker must therefore lock real capital or spend time producing work that survives review, while risking loss of stake for fraud; the horizon of repeated checks makes cheap, short-lived Sybils uneconomic.
